editorial.marketOverview: The US cash market is closed Saturday. Reuters' November 20 closing report puts Nasdaq Composite at -5.28%, S&P 500 at -3.70%, and Dow at -1.93%; previously verified Nasdaq 100 -5.6% Friday and SOX approximately -11% characterize semiconductor-led risk-off trading. Friday VIX close 37.66 is historical, not a new Saturday quote. Nasdaq 100 weekly -10.4% was reported by FT. These returns are not independently tick-synchronized.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to Saturday 03:35 EST, Reuters' November 20 closing coverage and TD Economics' Nov 23–27 release calendar were rechecked. They corroborate already incorporated Friday losses and next-week event risk. No new verified Saturday catalyst, new curated Open Watch entry, or market observation warrants changing the bearish three-day path.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The severity of chip and broad-index declines, negative reported breadth and elevated VIX continue to support a bearish risk regime. Friday's rate relief did not reverse equity losses. The prior indicative 10Y 4.94% minus 2Y 4.65% equals +0.29 percentage points or +29 basis points, but those earlier quotes are stale and cannot be treated as a current synchronized curve; Reuters' later 10Y near 4.93% lacks a matched 2Y. Direct FedWatch, VXN and contract-matched oil futures remain unverified. No particular headline is assigned definitive causality for Friday's moves.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: elevated continuation risk, with potential sharp short-covering rebound; 09:45 ET US flash PMIs may affect yields and technology valuation. Tuesday November 24: 10:00 ET consumer confidence and AI-hardware earnings including Analog Devices and Dell may test semiconductor sentiment. Wednesday November 25: 08:30 ET concentrated GDP, personal income/spending and durable goods releases, plus 14:00 ET Fed Beige Book, can alter the path before Thanksgiving. These are scheduled catalysts, not known market responses.
editorial.bullCase: Deep oversold conditions and high protection demand allow a powerful countertrend rebound if QQQ and SOX/SMH rise together, breadth broadens and VIX/VXN decline. A synchronized fall in Treasury yields could support duration-sensitive tech, but the relevant current pair is unavailable.
editorial.bearCase: Nasdaq 100 bear-market drawdown, Friday's unusually sharp semiconductor losses, broad risk aversion and elevated VIX leave rallies vulnerable to selling. Hot inflation, higher yields or disappointing AI hardware guidance are conditional downside scenarios, not observed future outcomes.
